subject: Security intake & scope prioritization for Cora Health
messages:
From: Tessa Morgan <tessa.morgan@redwoodinference.com>
To: Meghan Stokes <meghan.stokes@corahealth.com>, Jordan Price <jordan.price@corahealth.com>
Cc: Avery Johnson <avery.johnson@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Sat, 12 Dec 2026 14:05:00 -0800
Subject: Security intake & scope prioritization for Cora Health

Thanks again for the call today — quick recap and proposed next steps so we keep momentum.

Highlights from our discussion:
- Current state: you confirmed an internal controls program; SOC 2 Type II was performed but you weren’t sure of the exact audit period (you asked us to request the report).
- Compliance drivers: protecting PHI for payer integrations (HIPAA requirements) and EU data residency considerations (GDPR) for onboarding EU pilot customers.
- Certification interest: short-term priority is SOC 2 scope confirmation and evidence for procurement; medium-term interest in ISO 27001 for client trust; long-term consideration for FedRAMP if pursuing federal contracts.

Proposed immediate plan (risk-and-effort prioritized):
1) Vendor security questionnaire (attached) — please complete the highlighted tabs for the controls we discussed (network, encryption, data flows). Target: return within 7 business days (by 2026-12-21).
2) SOC 2 artifact request — if you can share the most recent Type II report or an SOC summary, we’ll map overlap to our customer-impact controls. I attached our public SOC 2 report for reference.
3) Two-phase roadmap suggestion: Phase A (SOC Scope + Evidence bundle) — <8 weeks to answer procurement questions and provide an evidence pack; Phase B (ISO assessment scoping / FedRAMP feasibility) — follow-on planning session.

Action items from Redwood:
- I (Tessa) will coordinate the questionnaire and intake and schedule a 30-min follow-up to review your answers (suggested week of 12/28).
- Avery will produce a quick mapping doc showing control overlap between your SOC artifacts and common HIPAA/GDPR asks.
- Once we have the returned questionnaire, we’ll propose a prioritized artifact list for rapid procurement responses.

Attachments: Vendor_Security_Questionnaire_CoraHealth.xlsx; Redwood_SOC2_Report_2024.pdf

If that looks right, please confirm timeline and add Jordan or anyone else on your security team to the thread.

Thanks — Tessa
Tessa Morgan
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
(415) 555-0132
https://redwoodinference.com

From: Meghan Stokes <meghan.stokes@corahealth.com>
To: Tessa Morgan <tessa.morgan@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Jordan Price <jordan.price@corahealth.com>
Date: Sat, 12 Dec 2026 16:18:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Security intake & scope prioritization for Cora Health

Thanks Tessa — helpful recap. A couple quick clarifications: 
- SOC 2 status: we have a SOC 2 Type II completed for the period Jul 2025–Jun 2026 (vendor shared with procurement last quarter). I can surface the PDF but will need approval from procurement to share externally — Jordan is on that.
- HIPAA / PHI: our product stores limited patient identifiers for scheduling and claims mapping. We need to ensure any FedRAMP conversation is scoped correctly because PHI tends to require stricter controls and potential BAAs.
- GDPR: we have an EU data flow diagram and a Data Processing Addendum; we will include the DPA and the EU flow diagram as part of our response.

Procurement timeline: they want a first-pass evidence bundle by mid-Jan to attach to a vendor checklist. If you can turn your questionnaire and the SOC mapping into a short deliverable, that would be ideal.

I’ll try to get the SOC 2 PDF to you this week but if procurement delays it, I’ll at least push a SOC summary and the DPA.

—Meghan
Meghan Stokes
Head of Integrations, Cora Health
meghan.stokes@corahealth.com

From: Tessa Morgan <tessa.morgan@redwoodinference.com>
To: Meghan Stokes <meghan.stokes@corahealth.com>, Jordan Price <jordan.price@corahealth.com>
Cc: Avery Johnson <avery.johnson@redwoodinference.com>, Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Sun, 13 Dec 2026 08:22:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Security intake & scope prioritization for Cora Health

Appreciate the clarity, Meghan — that timeline works and explains the procurement gating. A couple quick notes and a suggested prioritization: 

1) If SOC 2 Type II PDF is delayed, the SOC summary + DPA + EU flow diagram is sufficient for an initial mapping. We’ll flag any high-risk gaps that would block procurement (encryption at rest/in transit, access controls, logging).

2) Suggested prioritization for our joint roadmap: 
   - Immediate (Procurement): complete questionnaire + SOC mapping (deliverable to procurement by 2027-01-12).
   - Short term (Trust): produce an evidence bundle and a short controls memo for your security reviewers (2–3 weeks after questionnaire return).
   - Medium term (Cert planning): if you want ISO 27001 next, we can run a gap assessment and build an ISO-friendly controls backlog; FedRAMP feasibility will need a separate scoping call because of federal FedRAMP baselines and potential impact on hosting.

3) Meeting: proposing a 30-min intake review on Tue 2026-12-29 10:00am PT — please confirm availability or suggest alternate.

I’ve uploaded the questionnaire and a draft certification roadmap to a shared folder: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1A2b3CExample

Next steps from our side: Avery will start the SOC-to-procurement mapping; Vivek (cc’d) — our security lead — can weigh in on any potential PHI-related control gaps and evidence we should prioritize.

Thanks — looking forward to the intake review.

Tessa
Account Executive, Redwood Inference

From: Tessa Morgan <tessa.morgan@redwoodinference.com>
To: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwoodinference.com>, Avery Johnson <avery.johnson@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Sun, 13 Dec 2026 09:42:00 -0800
Subject: Fwd: Security intake & scope prioritization for Cora Health — quick intake ask

Vivek / Avery — forwarding the thread from the intake with Cora Health. High level: SOC 2 Type II exists (Jul 2025–Jun 2026), they store limited PHI, procurement wants evidence mid-Jan.

Could you both do a 30-min intake review today or tomorrow? Specific asks: 
- Quick risk flag: major control gaps vs HIPAA that would block procurement (focus on encryption, BAAs, and logging/retention).
- Evidence bundling: list the minimum artifacts we should ask Cora for to satisfy procurement (SOC summary, DPA, encryption configuration screenshots, user access matrix, incident response runbook).
- Questionnaire sprints: advise which questionnaire tabs we should prioritize answering first so procurement has what they need by 2027-01-12.

I’ll prepare the HubSpot deal note (RDW-4721) and include links to the folder. If you want me to draft any of the artifact request language to send to Meghan, I can do that after the intake call.

Thanks — Tessa
